ProjectSpecification__Description: Project specification notes for the TrueVision drawings. Groups hold notes in order; a note’s code is its group’s prefix and its place in the group (GN01, EE02), so the order is the truth and Note__Code is written for readers and recomputed on every load. Specification bubbles on the Layout Editor sheets link to notes by Note__Id. General groups are listed on every sheet’s notes margin, after the notes that sheet’s bubbles link to. LastIdNumber only ever goes up, so no id is used twice.

Group__Notes.Note__Body: Drawings describe the proposed development for planning assessment. They are not construction drawings or a complete Building Regulations specification. Obtain coordinated construction details, structural calculations and Building Control approval before relevant work starts. Refer discrepancies to Noble Architecture before proceeding.

Site information derived from a photogrammetric aerial survey of the holding, with purchased Ordnance Survey data to the site plans. No measured building survey of the existing dwelling has been carried out. Proposed buildings are derived from Noble Architecture's three-dimensional model. Do not scale from these drawings. Verify all dimensions on site.
Issued for pre-application advice. Materials, dimensions and levels are indicative at this stage and to be fixed before a planning application.

ProjectSpecification__Groups.Group__Title: Building Features  -  North West Elevation  -  Main House

Group__Notes.Note__Body: Central entrance: six-panel painted timber door with narrow sidelights, on cut ashlar jambs standing on plinth blocks. A deep moulded entablature with projecting cornice sits above, and a semicircular radial fanlight above that, framed by concentric moulded archivolts.

Canted bays flank the entrance, in cut ashlar throughout, with a moulded cornice and blocking course at the head. French doors to the centre face and sashes to the splayed returns, opening onto the terrace.
First floor painted timber sashes in moulded surrounds, with two hipped dormers above within the roof slope.
Orangery between the house and the kitchen building: painted timber, glazed the full height of its bays, under a bespoke glazed lantern.
Kitchen building gable: two tall arched openings with radial fanlights in cut ashlar surrounds. Stone chimney stack against the gable.

ProjectSpecification__Groups.Group__Title: Building Features  -  South East Elevation  -  Main House

Group__Notes.Note__Body: Central entrance: a pair of Tuscan columns on plinth blocks carry a full entablature with a projecting moulded cornice. Beneath it a six-panel painted timber door with a semicircular radial fanlight, dressed in cut ashlar and approached over stone steps. The porch projects slightly from the wall plane.

Tripartite ground floor windows flank the entrance beneath cambered heads with moulded ashlar surrounds, and are the tallest openings on the building. First floor sashes are shorter and set in plainer surrounds.
Hipped roof with three hipped dormers lighting the second floor. Dormer cheek and roof finish to be confirmed before a full application.
Low hipped glazed lantern set astride the main ridge at the centre of the house. Frame material and finish to be confirmed before a full application.

Single-storey colonnade entrance to the right of the main block: Tuscan columns flanking a glazed painted timber door, with flat ashlar lintels over the windows either side, beneath a flat roof with a moulded cornice. Leads through to the kitchen building and the coach house.
Kitchen building gable above the colonnade entrance: moulded raking cornice, with a circular opening set in cut ashlar with four projecting keyblocks. Stone chimney stack rises behind.

ProjectSpecification__Groups.Group__Title: Building Features  -  North East Elevation  -  Main House

Group__Notes.Note__Body: The house is seen above the coach house range on this elevation: hipped roof with two hipped dormers and the moulded eaves cornice returning on this side.

ProjectSpecification__Groups.Group__Title: Building Features  -  South West Elevation  -  Main House

Group__Notes.Note__Body: Three arched openings in a recessed bay at ground floor. Tuscan columns, with matching responds returned against the flanking walls, carry a full entablature with plain frieze and projecting cornice. French doors beneath radial fanlights to each arch. The arcade is recessed within the wall plane and does not project beyond the elevation.
Larger windows flank the arcade at both levels, with three hipped dormers above within the roof slope.
Kitchen building: three pairs of painted timber French doors with moulded cornice heads, beneath a run of flush rooflights in the roof slope. Eaves sit below the eaves of the house.

Coursed squared natural stone to all external walls of the house, the kitchen building and the coach house. Cut ashlar of the same stone to the plinth, quoins, window and door surrounds, cills, eaves cornice, canted bays, entrance compositions and the carriage arch. Stone type and source to be confirmed before a full application.
All columns and pilasters are of the Tuscan order in cut ashlar: the entrance porch, the loggia arcade and the colonnade entrance.
Natural stone slate laid to diminishing courses to all pitched roofs. Stone slate type, and whether new or reclaimed, to be confirmed before a full application.
Natural stone chimney stacks with moulded caps to the house, the kitchen building and the coach house.
Conservation pattern rooflights set flush within the roof plane to the kitchen building and the coach house. Product to be confirmed before a full application.
External joinery painted timber with slender glazing bars, to a single pattern across every building in the group. Pane configuration and paint colour to be confirmed before a full application.
Painted timber six-panel entrance doors with radial fanlights to the house. French doors to the loggia, the terraces and the orangery. Boarded and strapped timber doors to the coach house.

ProjectSpecification__Groups.Group__Title: Building Features  -  North East Elevation  -  Coach House

Group__Notes.Note__Body: Long single-storey range under a continuous pitched roof, with accommodation lit from within the roof slope.

Central gabled bay carries a semicircular carriage arch turned in voussoirs with a projecting keystone, on cut ashlar imposts with quoined jambs. The arch carries the pedestrian and service route through from the courtyard.
Circular louvred oculus in the gable above the arch, set in a cut ashlar surround with four projecting keyblocks.

Cupola on the ridge above the gable: square base with an arched louvred opening and a moulded cornice, pyramidal roof, ball finial and weathervane. Material and finish to be confirmed before a full application.
Segmentally headed two-light painted timber windows with cut ashlar cills to the range.

ProjectSpecification__Groups.Group__Title: Building Features  -  South West Elevation  -  Coach House

Group__Notes.Note__Body: The carriage arch returns on the courtyard face in matching voussoirs with quoined jambs. Gable oculus and cupola as CE03 and CE04.
Courtyard face: boarded and strapped painted timber doors hung either side of glazed French doors beneath a cambered head. Segmentally headed window with a cut ashlar cill to the range beyond.
South east end gable: boarded timber loft door set high in the gable, with a cut ashlar cill and quoined angles.
